definitions.explanation: tending to talk a lot or use many words

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{多弁|たべん}な{人|ひと}だ。
お{酒|さけ}を{飲|の}むと{多弁|たべん}になる。
examples.english: I become talkative when I drink.

examples.japanese: {普段|ふだん}{無口|むくち}な{彼|かれ}が{今日|きょう}は{多弁|たべん}だ。
examples.english: He's usually quiet, but he's talkative today.

notes:
COMPOUND:
{多|た} (many) + {弁|べん} (speech)

NUANCE:
Can be neutral or slightly negative depending on context. Unlike {お喋|しゃべ}り, which is casual and often affectionate, {多弁|たべん} is more formal and can imply excessive talking.

CONTRAST:
- {多弁|たべん} (talkative) ↔ {寡黙|かもく} (taciturn)
- {多弁|たべん} ↔ {無口|むくち} (quiet, untalkative)

RELATED:
- {雄弁|ゆうべん} - eloquent
- {能弁|のうべん} - fluent, articulate
- {饒舌|じょうぜつ} - garrulous, verbose
- お{喋|しゃべ}り - chatty (casual)
